subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm planning a static vehicle model as a single TS module, sketching out dimensions for the hull (~12m length, 3m width, 2.2m height) and six wheels sized around 0.65m radius, built from boxes and cylinders without needing joints.

I'm now working out the layout details: a long railgun barrel mounted on top extending forward, four angled stabilizer legs with foot pads touching the ground, and a color palette of olive, gunmetal, tan, steel, rubber, and a cyan glow accent. Positioning the wheels along the hull using rotated cylinders for the tires...

Adding wheel hubs, mudguards, and axle housings, then building up the main chassis as a lower hull box with a sloped front cab and tilted windscreen, with the railgun capping the rear.

Now I'm laying out the capacitor bank deck with glowing cylindrical capacitors, the turret pivot ring, and the railgun's twin parallel rails with ribbed insulators and a glowing core between them, plus breech block and muzzle brake — deciding to keep the gun horizontal rather than dealing with rotating every part for a pitch angle.

I'm positioning the gun mount higher above the cab roof with trunnion cheeks and a cradle housing bridging deck to rail height, checking clearances so the rail bottom sits above the cab roof, and adding a saddle-shaped front support on the cab roof. Now I'm working out stabilizer leg placement at the hull corners, spacing them to avoid colliding with the wheel positions along the hull.

I'm sketching the outrigger legs as horizontal beams extending from the hull sides out to foot pads, with piston-style vertical struts and diagonal braces, checking they clear the wheels and adding foot pad geometry and hazard striping. Now I'm planning the remaining surface details — headlights, armor plates, side skirts, stowage boxes, antenna, radar dish, roof sensors, exhaust stacks, and glowing accent details.

Writing helper functions...

Adding a glowing teal glass roof, side windows, and front headlights with yellow-white glow, plus a bumper detail...

Now I'm planning the rear deck layout - placing a capacitor bank behind the cradle, arranging vertical cylindrical capacitors on either side of the centerline at staggered depths toward the back of the vehicle.

I'm also positioning a generator housing box on the deck closer to the front, giving it vents and exhaust stacks, with cheek panels flanking it on either side.

For the radar dish, I'm using a partial sphere geometry to form a curved scoop shape, mounting it on a mast cylinder near the generator's rear corner and rotating it to face outward.

Now I'm working out the rails along the track, sizing them and positioning insulator blocks across both rails at regular one-unit intervals.

For the breech I'm adding a chunkier box near the back plus coil elements along the rails using torus geometry oriented to naturally ring around the barrel axis, spaced evenly along z.

I should check that the coil rings clear the rails in radius and height before adding six of them, glowing cyan and centered at the rail height. Then I want to add details like a ladder, hatch, chevron stripe emblem, and hazard stripes on the feet, plus tire tread using small boxes arranged in a ring around each wheel -- though with twelve treads per wheel across six wheels that's a lot of parts, so I'll keep it moderate.

Working out tread box positions and rotations around each wheel...

Adding lug bolts as tiny boxes around each hub, then placing axle boxes connecting the wheels across the body.

Still detailing the leg geometry...

Checking fender placement against beam and wheels to confirm no clipping, then moving on to write the final code.
